'''Augustin Banyaga''' (born March 31, 1947) is a [[Rwanda]]n-born [[United States|America]]n [[mathematician]] whose research fields include [[symplectic topology]] and [[contact geometry]]. He is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].

==Biography==
While at the [[University of Geneva]], he earned a [[B.S.]] degree in 1971 and an [[M.S.]] in 1972.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/banyaga_augustin.html |title=Mathematicians of the African Diaspora |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=University of Buffalo, Department of Mathematics |publisher= |access-date=November 26, 2024 |quote=}}</ref> He earned his [[Ph.D.]] degree in 1976 at the [[University of Geneva]] under the supervision of [[André Haefliger]].<ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy |id=40660}}</ref>  (Banyaga was the first person from Rwanda to obtain a Ph.D. in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Celebratio Mathematica]]| url=https://celebratio.org/Banyaga_A/article/753/|title=Interview with Augustin Banyaga|author=Allyn Jackson|year=2020}}</ref>) He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] (1977–1978),<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=8 Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106144422/http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=8 |date=January 6, 2013 }}</ref> [[Benjamin Peirce]] Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]] (1978–1982), and assistant professor at [[Boston University]] (1982–1984), before joining the faculty at Pennsylvania State University in 1984 as associate professor.  He was promoted to full professor in 1992.

In 2009 Banyaga was elected a Fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]], and in 2015 he was named a Distinguished Senior Scholar by [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Augustin Banyaga named Distinguished Senior Scholar {{!}} Penn State University|url=https://news.psu.edu/story/357107/2015/05/11/academics/augustin-banyaga-named-distinguished-senior-scholar|access-date=2020-06-10|website=news.psu.edu|language=en}}</ref>

He has made significant contributions in symplectic topology, especially on the structure of [[Group (mathematics)|groups]] of [[diffeomorphism]]s preserving a symplectic form ([[symplectomorphism]]s).  One of his best-known results states that the group of [[Hamiltonian vector field|Hamiltonian]] diffeomorphisms of a [[compact space|compact]], [[Connectedness|connected]], [[symplectic manifold]] is a [[simple group]]; in particular, it does not admit any non-trivial [[homomorphism]] to the real line.

Banyaga is an editor of ''[[Afrika Matematica]]'', the journal of the [[African Mathematical Union]], and an editor of the African Journal of Mathematics.  He has supervised the theses of 9 Ph.D. students.<ref name="MG"/>
